# kronos-docs

Official Kronos ORM documentation at [kotlinorm.com](https://kotlinorm.com), built with Angular 21, NgDoc 21, Transloco, PrimeNG and Tailwind CSS.

## Development

Use Node.js 22 LTS or 24 LTS and pnpm 10.30.2, as declared in `package.json`.

```bash
corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
corepack pnpm start
```

The development server runs at `http://localhost:3307`. `corepack pnpm` selects the declared package-manager version without changing a globally installed pnpm.

## Source and generated files

- `src/app/docs/{en,zh-CN}/`: mirrored Markdown pages, category/page metadata and examples. Shared Nunjucks macros live in `src/app/docs/macros/`.
- `src/app/locale/`: locale policy and the single language service, shared by the homepage, blog, documentation and search. Documentation URL language takes precedence; switching language keeps the page, query parameters and heading fragment.
- `src/app/routes/documentation/`: layout container, theme lifecycle, NgDoc link compatibility and the Markdown copy control.
- `src/app/search-policy.ts` and `doc-search-engine.ts`: language-isolated ranking, bounded result excerpts and cached index loading.
- `src/assets/{blogs,i18n,images,icons}/`: localized blog posts, application translations and static assets.
- `scripts/`: route/link checks, static documentation generation, output verification and the production-site merge.
- `ng-doc/`: NgDoc-generated TypeScript and content; do not edit it.
- `docs/`: Angular bundles, readable static documentation, search index, sitemap and redirects; generated by `pnpm build`.
- `dist/site/`: complete deployment output including Dokka API documentation; generated by `deploy-docs.sh`.

Write ordinary usage pages for the current API. Keep version changes and upgrade history in the bilingual release-notes pages.

## Verification and build

```bash
corepack pnpm test:policies
corepack pnpm check:links
corepack pnpm build
corepack pnpm run test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless
```

`test:policies` covers locale and search behavior, broken route/link cases and deployment merging. `check:links` verifies bilingual routes, category/page ordering and source links. The default Angular test suite checks rendered navigation, language bootstrap, search updates, clipboard behavior and sidebar controls. Set `CHROME_BIN` to the installed Chrome executable when Karma cannot locate it.

`pnpm build` runs NgDoc and Angular, generates static pages from the same compiled NgDoc content, and verifies every static route/anchor, code alternative, table, canonical/alternate link, search entry and sitemap route. Use `pnpm check:static` to repeat the output verification without rebuilding. Run the complete Angular suite after NgDoc generation; `pnpm test:architecture` provides an isolated behavior check while generated pages are being rebuilt.

The required `Build documentation site` CI check runs for every pull request to `main`. It also builds all eight module API sites, verifies their README content and local links, and merges the complete deployment output.

Static pages are directly accessible at `/documentation/en/getting-started/kmp/` and `/documentation/zh-CN/getting-started/kmp/`. They include readable code, tables, heading links and links between languages. The interactive application remains accessible at `/#/documentation/...`; each static page links to its matching interactive page. `DOCS_SITE_URL` selects the canonical site origin during the build and defaults to `https://kotlinorm.com`.

To preview the generated static pages and interactive application locally:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3309 --directory docs
```

Open `http://localhost:3309/documentation/en/getting-started/kmp/` or `http://localhost:3309/#/documentation/en/getting-started/kmp`.

## Complete site and deployment

Use JDK 21 for the Kotlin build and documentation scripts, alongside the website's Node.js/pnpm dependencies. The script launcher prepares the catalogued Kotlin SDK automatically.

```bash
./deploy-docs.sh
```

This generates module API documentation through `scripts/run quality dokka`, builds the website, and merges the outputs into `dist/site/` through `scripts/merge-site.mjs`. `/api/*` keeps the Dokka files accessible, exact static documentation routes come next, and the final redirect handles the interactive application.

For Cloudflare Pages, use:

- Root directory: `kronos-docs`
- Build command: `./deploy-docs.sh`
- Build output directory: `dist/site`
